audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[2] instructs the player to 'Pop R the instant her R (Lilting Lullaby) puts you to sleep'. You cannot cast Divine Judgment while asleep. Separately, Blooming Blows' edge true damage and Swirlseed's ability to roll into your retreat are absent.
audit.why: Riot's text says enemies become Drowsy before falling asleep — the Drowsy window is the only moment the ultimate is castable, and the page points the player at the moment after it. Following it literally means eating the whole follow-up with R unspent. The true damage matters because the page's answer to poke is Q's resist shred and W sustain, and neither touches the edge damage. Swirlseed cutting a dashless Kayle's retreat is a Flash decision.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to pop R during the Drowsy window, before the sleep lands. Blooming Blows' edge true damage written into whys[1] and early; Swirlseed and 'hold Flash for the wall, not the damage' added to early.
sources: enemyKit R text (Drowsy before falling asleep)

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1 and 2 read Kayle in both layers while the whys beneath them say the opposite — whys[1] has her out-poking your melee autos, whys[2] literally ends 'concede the trade'. Row 4 reads Skill while whys[4] and mid both say level 6 flips the lane hard in your favour. The packet agrees with the prose on all three.
audit.why: Levels 2-3 are Kayle at melee range against a 450-range spin with a move-speed kite; level 6 is where Divine Ascent's ranged tier arrives and the poke stops being free.
audit.corrected: phases[1..2].side and win[1..2] set to Lillia; phases[4].side and win[4] set to Kayle. Three matched pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's defect is real — zero cooldown numbers anywhere in either layer, while 'track Blooming Blows' is repeated a dozen times.
audit.why: Blooming Blows is 6s at rank 1 falling to 4s; it is not a cooldown you wait out, and a player told to 'engage when it is down' will wait for a window that never opens. Watch Out! Eep! at 14s and Lilting Lullaby at 150s are the timers that actually gate her.
audit.corrected: 6s Q, 14s W and 150s R written into whys[1], whys[2], early and wants.foe[1].

audit.why: 54.39% over 353 games, consistent with a scaling win from level 6.

edits.before: Lillia is one of the few enemies who can actually poke your weak early lane — her Q (Blooming Blows) spin and passive burn chip you while you are stuck at melee range with only Q and one point of W sustain, and her W (Watch Out! Eep!) bonk punishes any greedy walk-up. Do not chase her; she kites with Q move speed and you will eat free burn damage walking after her. Last-hit with Q (Radiant Blast) at range to shred a little of her resist and slow her, accept the poke, and W-heal it back when she disengages. Your only goal these levels is to reach 6 without giving up a kill — never let her bait you forward into a W bonk and R sleep.
edits.after: Lillia is one of the few enemies who can actually poke your weak early lane — her Q (Blooming Blows) spin and passive burn chip you while you are stuck at melee range with only Q and one point of W sustain, and the spin's outer edge is true damage, so no resist you buy answers it. Her W (Watch Out! Eep!, 14s) bonk punishes any greedy walk-up. Do not chase her; she kites with Q move speed and you eat free burn walking after her. Last-hit with Q (Radiant Blast) at range, accept the poke, and W-heal it back when she disengages. Reach 6 without giving up a kill, and hold Flash for a Swirlseed rolling into your retreat, not for the damage.

notes: The wants.you[2] line was actively harmful — it told the player to use Divine Judgment at a moment they are unable to cast. Fixed to the Drowsy window, which Riot's own R text describes. Rows 1, 2 and 4 flipped to agree with both the packet and the whys already printed under them. Mirror (lillia__kayle) not yet audited.
